Experimental results show good agreement with numerical simulations. The resulting asymmetric circular Airy derivative beams (ACADBs), combining strong abrupt autofocusing with extreme DOF, offer promising applications in optical trapping, optical communications, microfabrication, and biomedical imaging.
tldr: This paper studies enhanced autofocusing and depth-of-focus in circular Airy derivative beams via controlled asymmetry, with applications in optical trapping and communications.
motivation: To improve the performance of circular Airy beams for applications requiring strong focusing and extended depth-of-focus.
method: The authors introduce controlled asymmetry to merge multiple discrete autofocusing events into a single elongated focal region, and experimentally demonstrate the effect.
result: Depth-of-focus is extended by up to 400% with a 32% improvement in autofocusing ability, or autofocusing ability enhanced by up to 193% with nearly unchanged depth-of-focus.
conclusion: Asymmetric circular Airy derivative beams offer a promising combination of strong abrupt autofocusing and extreme depth-of-focus for various applications.

title: Matrix-free Phase-field Modeling Of Fracture In Micromechanical Testing Simulations Of Inelastic Materials
authors: Fabio Di Gioacchino, Rezgar Shakeri, Zachary Atkins, Karen Stengel, Layla Ghaffari, Jeremy Thompson, Jed Brown
abstract: ArXiv:2607.21150v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Resolving steep damage gradients across diffuse cracks in the phase-field modeling of fracture favors the use of high-order finite elements, for which matrix-free methods can provide superior performance and scalability. Here, we implement the Peric & Dettmer constitutive framework for visco-elastoplastic materials in an open source solid mechanics library supporting matrix-free operators for high-order finite elements with p-multigrid preconditioning on GPUs. We introduce a rheological fracture element assembled in series so that inelastic and fracture properties can appear to affect each other only at homogenization length scales. Numerical simulations of tensile and compressive tests are conducted for synthetic particle-matrix microstructures on an El Capitan high performance computing prototype. Results are shown to reproduce characteristic inelastic responses and crack propagation patterns.
tldr: This paper presents a matrix-free phase-field model for fracture in visco-elastoplastic materials, focusing on high-performance computing simulations of micromechanical tests.
motivation: Resolving steep damage gradients in phase-field fracture modeling requires high-order finite elements, which are computationally expensive; matrix-free methods offer better performance and scalability.
method: The authors implement the Peric & Dettmer constitutive framework in an open-source solid mechanics library with matrix-free operators for high-order finite elements and p-multigrid preconditioning on GPUs, introducing a rheological fracture element assembled in series.
result: Numerical simulations of tensile and compressive tests on synthetic particle-matrix microstructures reproduce characteristic inelastic responses and crack propagation patterns.
conclusion: The matrix-free approach enables efficient high-order finite element simulations of fracture in inelastic materials, suitable for large-scale computing.

title: Sharp Bounds On Diminished Sombor Index
authors: Meysam Taheri-Dehkordi, Amir Hossein Nokhodkar, Gholam Hossein Fath-Tabar
abstract: ArXiv:2607.20562v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Diminished Sombor index [MATH] of a simple graph [MATH] is a recently introduced degree-based topological index, defined as \[ DSO(G)= \sum_{uv\in E(G)} } {d_u+d_v} \] In this paper, we establish a collection of new sharp bounds for the [MATH] index in terms of several fundamental graph parameters and well-known topological indices. In all cases, the proposed bounds rigorously specify the equality conditions, thereby providing a complete characterization of the extremal graphs. These findings deepen the theoretical understanding of the [MATH] index and provide powerful analytical tools for interdisciplinary applications in mathematical chemistry.
tldr: This paper derives sharp bounds for the Diminished Sombor index, a degree-based topological index for simple graphs, with complete characterization of extremal graphs.
motivation: The Diminished Sombor index is a recently introduced topological index in mathematical chemistry, and establishing its bounds helps in understanding its theoretical properties and applications.
method: The authors use combinatorial and algebraic techniques to relate the DSO index to other graph parameters and topological indices, deriving inequalities and identifying equality conditions.
result: A collection of new sharp bounds for the DSO index is established, expressed in terms of fundamental graph parameters and well-known topological indices, with explicit extremal graphs.
conclusion: The findings deepen the theoretical understanding of the Diminished Sombor index and provide analytical tools for applications in mathematical chemistry.

title: Counting, Symmetries And Equivalence Classes Of Sudoku Grids
authors: Fernanda Pereira
abstract: ArXiv:2607.20669v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sudoku is a widely popular puzzle whose complete grids have been enumerated computationally: there are approximately [MATH] of them and, up to symmetry and renaming of digits, [MATH] essentially different ones. The classical enumeration reduces the count to [MATH] equivalence classes of the first band through a chain of ad hoc reductions, leaving the number [MATH] without any apparent structural explanation. We present an alternative derivation of these [MATH] classes, in which they arise as isomorphism classes of unordered triples (multisets) of column partitions under relabeling, a single invariant that replaces the original chain of reductions. This invariant makes it possible to apply Burnside's Lemma by hand: we recover [MATH], together with two intermediate stages of the classical reduction, through a closed derivation requiring no computational enumeration.
tldr: This paper presents a combinatorial derivation of the number of essentially different Sudoku grids using Burnside's Lemma and a novel invariant based on column partitions.
motivation: The classical enumeration of Sudoku grids relies on ad hoc reductions and computational enumeration; the authors seek a structural explanation for the number of equivalence classes.
method: The authors introduce an invariant that captures isomorphism classes of unordered triples of column partitions under relabeling, then apply Burnside's Lemma by hand to derive the count.
result: They recover the known number of 5,472,730,538 essentially different Sudoku grids and two intermediate stages of the classical reduction through a closed derivation.
conclusion: The work provides a more elegant and explanatory derivation of the Sudoku grid count, but it is purely combinatorial and unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: First-Order Analysis Of Optimization In Uniformly Convex Metric Spaces: Directional Subderivatives And Basic Descent
authors: D. Russell Luke, Titus Pinta, Qinyu Yan
abstract: ArXiv:2607.20677v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop tools for the analysis and implementation of explicit first-order methods for minimizing functions in uniformly convex metric spaces. We formulate sufficient conditions for convergence of descent sequences in terms of directional subderivatives, function values and iterates under regularity assumptions including boundedness, geodesic smoothness and a metric Polyak-{\L}ojasiewicz property. We show that there exists a steepest descent direction in which the assumptions for convergence are satisfied. This work provides a foundation for first-order explicit algorithms for locally smooth, nonconvex optimization.
tldr: This paper develops first-order optimization methods for uniformly convex metric spaces, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The paper aims to extend first-order optimization techniques to non-Euclidean metric spaces, which is a topic in mathematical optimization.
method: The authors formulate sufficient conditions for convergence using directional subderivatives, geodesic smoothness, and a metric Polyak-Łojasiewicz property.
result: They show existence of a steepest descent direction satisfying convergence assumptions, providing a foundation for explicit first-order algorithms.
conclusion: The work contributes to optimization theory but is unrelated to the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Convergence And Mixed-precision Preconditioning For The Naive Jacobi Eigenvalue Algorithm
authors: Erna Begovic, Marija Miloloza Pandur, Ana Perkovic
abstract: ArXiv:2607.20749v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The paper studies a Jacobi-type method for the eigenvalue problem of general complex matrices with simple eigenvalues. The method applies elementary triangular similarity transformations in order to annihilate selected off-diagonal elements and, when convergent, produces highly accurate eigenvalues. We give a new proof of its asymptotic quadratic convergence and derive an explicit, verifiable bound that describes the region in which this convergence is guaranteed. To make the method applicable well beyond matrices already close to the diagonal form, we introduce a preconditioning strategy. We use two types of preconditioners, both based on theoretical convergence results. The preconditioner is computed at lower precision to reduce computational cost, the associated similarity transformation is applied either at working or at higher precision, to preserve spectral information, while the main algorithm performs at working precision. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the resulting algorithm is robust and produces very accurate eigenvalues.
tldr: This paper presents a Jacobi-type eigenvalue algorithm for general complex matrices with convergence analysis and mixed-precision preconditioning.
motivation: To improve the efficiency and accuracy of eigenvalue computation for matrices not close to diagonal form.
method: The method uses elementary triangular similarity transformations to annihilate off-diagonal elements, with a preconditioning strategy computed at lower precision.
result: The algorithm achieves asymptotic quadratic convergence and produces highly accurate eigenvalues, as demonstrated by numerical experiments.
conclusion: The proposed preconditioned Jacobi method is robust and efficient for computing eigenvalues of general complex matrices.

title: A Virtual Element Method For Darcy's Problem Coupled With A Heat Equation
authors: Felipe Lepe Danilo Amigo
abstract: ArXiv:2607.20755v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In two dimensions, we develop a virtual element method to solve the Darcy's problem coupled with a nonlinear heat equation. This coupled model may allow for thermal diffusion and viscosity as a function of temperature. Under standard discretization assumptions and appropriate assumptions on the data, we prove the well posedness of the proposed numerical scheme. We also derive optimal error estimates under suitable regularity assumptions for the solution and appropriate assumptions on the data. We conclude with a series of numerical tests performed on different families of meshes that complement the theoretical findings.
tldr: This paper develops a virtual element method for solving Darcy's problem coupled with a nonlinear heat equation.
motivation: The authors aim to provide a numerical scheme for a coupled flow and heat transfer problem, which is important in geoscience and engineering applications.
method: They propose a virtual element discretization in two dimensions, prove well-posedness and optimal error estimates under standard assumptions, and validate with numerical tests.
result: The numerical scheme is proven to be well-posed and achieves optimal convergence rates on various mesh families.
conclusion: The virtual element method is effective for solving the coupled Darcy-heat problem, with theoretical guarantees and numerical evidence.

title: A Safeguarded Projected-Gradient Framework For Complementarity-Constrained Least-Squares Problems
authors: Lianghai Xiao, Wei Zhang, Jiayi Zhong
abstract: ArXiv:2607.20786v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Generalized absolute value equations (GAVEs) and linear complementarity problems (LCPs) arise in many equilibrium and optimization models and can both be formulated as least-squares problems over the complementarity set. Building on this shared formulation, we propose a safeguarded projected-gradient framework for both classes with problem-dependent algebraic refinements. We analyze its convergence properties and, under stronger conditions, establish finite recovery of the unique solution. Numerical experiments on GAVE and LCP benchmarks illustrate the practical behavior of the framework, including its high final accuracy in the tested settings and its problem-dependent computational tradeoffs.
tldr: This paper proposes a safeguarded projected-gradient framework for solving complementarity-constrained least-squares problems, which are mathematical optimization problems unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Generalized absolute value equations and linear complementarity problems arise in equilibrium and optimization models, and solving them efficiently is important for many applications.
method: The authors develop a safeguarded projected-gradient method with problem-dependent algebraic refinements, and analyze its convergence properties.
result: Under stronger conditions, the method achieves finite recovery of the unique solution, and numerical experiments demonstrate high final accuracy on benchmarks.
conclusion: The proposed framework is effective for complementarity-constrained least-squares problems, but it is purely mathematical and has no connection to quantum information theory or thermodynamics.

title: Frames From Functional Calculus
authors: Ilya Krishtal, Javad Mashreghi, Brendan Miller
abstract: ArXiv:2607.20798v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce frames generated by applying families of functions to a diagonal operator through functional calculus, with diagonal entries forming a Carleson interpolating sequence. First, for separated spectra contained in a Stolz domain and an angular sector, we prove that systems of fractional operator powers remain frames whenever the step size satisfies the natural angular restriction. This extends earlier results for positive real spectra and permits noninteger powers. We also show that the angular restriction is sharp in general. Second, we give an [MATH]-perturbation criterion for frames generated by more general continuous functions, assuming a density condition on a curve containing the spectrum. The results broaden the class of structured frames available in dynamical sampling and related operator-orbit problems.
tldr: The paper introduces frames generated by functional calculus of diagonal operators with Carleson interpolating sequences, extending results to noninteger powers and general continuous functions.
motivation: To broaden the class of structured frames available in dynamical sampling and operator-orbit problems by using functional calculus.
method: The authors consider a diagonal operator with diagonal entries forming a Carleson interpolating sequence, and apply families of functions via functional calculus. They prove frame conditions for fractional powers under angular restrictions and give a perturbation criterion for general continuous functions.
result: Systems of fractional operator powers remain frames when the step size satisfies a natural angular restriction, which is shown to be sharp. A perturbation criterion for frames generated by more general continuous functions is also established.
conclusion: The results extend known frame constructions to noninteger powers and broader function classes, with potential applications in dynamical sampling.

title: Ball-Codifference Screening For Heavy-Tailed Predictors
authors: Vahed Maroufy Mohsen Rezapour
abstract: ArXiv:2607.20821v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: High-dimensional screening is commonly built on covariance, correlation, or least-squares measures. These summary measures can be unstable or even undefined, when predictors are sparse or have heavy-tailed distributions. Building on our recent work on extended codifference and the idea of Ball-covariance, we develop Ball-codifference for marginal screening in statistical modeling with heavy-tailed predictors and responses. The proposed statistic combines the rank-type geometry of random balls with the codifference as a dependency measure constructed based on the characteristic function, so it can be computed without requiring well-defined finite first or second moments. We define Ball-codifference and its normalized screening utility, and formulate a sure independence screening procedure. Large-sample normality follows from a bounded V-statistic and functional-delta-method argument under standard nondegeneracy and regularity conditions. Simulation studies under Gaussian and sub-Gaussian stable designs show that codifference-weighted Ball screening gives competitive or improved recovery of highly associated predictors, especially when tail heaviness is pronounced. Also, our data example illustrates that our variable screening method significantly improves prediction accuracy in linear regression.
tldr: This paper proposes a new screening method for heavy-tailed predictors using Ball-codifference, a dependency measure combining random balls and codifference.
motivation: High-dimensional screening methods based on covariance or correlation are unstable or undefined when predictors are heavy-tailed or sparse.
method: The authors develop Ball-codifference, which uses rank-type geometry of random balls and codifference based on characteristic functions, and formulate a sure independence screening procedure.
result: Simulations show competitive or improved recovery of associated predictors under heavy-tailed distributions, and a data example demonstrates improved prediction accuracy in linear regression.
conclusion: Ball-codifference screening is effective for heavy-tailed data where traditional methods fail.

title: Mean Field And N-agent Games For Optimal Relative Consumption-investment With Jump Risk And Common Noise
authors: Yiming Jiang, Fuxing Li, Yawei Wei, Zimeng Zheng
abstract: ArXiv:2607.20845v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies an optimal consumption--investment problem for competitive agents in an \(N\)-player game and its associated mean field game. Each agent invests in an individual risky asset subject to idiosyncratic noise, common noise and downward jump risk, and the interaction among agents is induced by relative performance concerns in both consumption and terminal wealth. In the mean field limit, we characterize a deterministic mean field equilibrium in analytical form by using the stochastic maximum principle. Numerical experiments are presented to illustrate the resulting equilibrium and its financial implications. Finally, based on the obtained mean field equilibrium, we construct an approximate Nash equilibrium for the \(N\)-player game. This model is motivated by and .
tldr: This paper studies optimal consumption-investment with relative performance concerns in a mean field game framework, unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The paper addresses competitive agents' consumption-investment decisions under jump risk and common noise, motivated by financial economics.
method: It uses stochastic maximum principle to derive a deterministic mean field equilibrium and constructs an approximate Nash equilibrium for the N-player game.
result: Analytical characterization of the mean field equilibrium and numerical experiments illustrating financial implications.
conclusion: The model provides insights into optimal strategies with relative performance concerns, but has no connection to quantum information theory or thermodynamics.

title: Structure-Preserving Spectral Dynamic Programming On Compact Lie Groups
authors: Yang Qi Shanqing Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.20854v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study spectral approximations of the dynamic programming semigroup for finite-horizon optimal control on a connected compact Lie group [MATH], and of the associated first-order Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation. The Bellman operator is monotone and non-expansive in the supremum norm, while the Peter-Weyl decomposition of [MATH], on which every Fourier method on [MATH] rests, is orthogonal, and the mismatch is quantitative. The natural sup-norm error recursion of the Galerkin iteration is amplified at every step by the Lebesgue constant of the spectral projection, which grows logarithmically on [MATH] and polynomially on compact Lie groups of rank one, including [MATH], and in computation the iteration violates elementary bounds within a few steps. We restore the dynamic programming structure at the discrete level by replacing the orthogonal projection with spectral filters of Markov type. An auxiliary heat-kernel/vanishing-viscosity scheme yields qualitative sup-norm convergence for Lipschitz data. The main result is a Fej\'er-type filter on [MATH], finite-rank, positivity preserving and non-expansive, together with a convergence theorem at the rate [MATH] for Lipschitz data, where [MATH] is the time step, [MATH] the spectral resolution and [MATH] the viscosity. The viscosity may be zero, and the coupling [MATH] then gives the rate [MATH]. The proof interprets the filter as a small random perturbation of the controlled dynamics, requires neither a priori regularity of the value function nor a consistency argument in the viscosity sense for the filtering step, and extends to a fully discrete realization based on positive cubature, with exact Wigner transport on [MATH]. Numerical experiments confirm the predicted rates and filter bias and quantify the frame dependence of two chart-based baselines.
tldr: This paper develops spectral dynamic programming methods for optimal control on compact Lie groups, using Markov-type filters to preserve monotonicity and non-expansiveness.
motivation: Standard spectral Galerkin methods for Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equations on compact Lie groups suffer from instability due to the Lebesgue constant, causing iteration bounds to be violated. The authors aim to restore the dynamic programming structure at the discrete level.
method: The authors replace orthogonal spectral projections with spectral filters of Markov type, specifically a Fejér-type filter on SU(2), and analyze a heat-kernel/vanishing-viscosity scheme to achieve sup-norm convergence.
result: They prove a convergence rate of O(Δt + h^r + ε) for Lipschitz data, where Δt is the time step, h the spectral resolution, and ε the viscosity, with the coupling ε = h^r giving rate O(Δt + h^r). Numerical experiments confirm the predicted rates.
conclusion: The proposed filter-based approach yields a stable, positivity-preserving, and non-expansive numerical scheme for optimal control on compact Lie groups, with rigorous convergence guarantees.

title: Implicit Primal-Dual Guarantees In Unconstrained First-Order Minimization
authors: Alex L. Wang Benjamin Grimmer
abstract: ArXiv:2607.20875v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work considers the design of first-order convex optimization algorithms and convergence proofs. In particular, we consider nonsmooth Lipschitz and smooth problems accessed through a subgradient or gradient oracle, respectively. For the general class of fixed-step first-order methods, prior work on Performance Estimation Problems (PEPs) has shown that structured, tight convergence proofs typically exist. Under mild conditions, we further show that any first-order method guaranteeing a bound on the primal objective gap [MATH] assuming only a bound on [MATH] actually has a stronger guarantee on an explicit, computable primal-dual gap at the same rate. These implicit optimal dual certificates, which take the form of affine lower bounds, also provide insight into the role of auxiliary sequences in momentum methods.
tldr: This paper studies convergence guarantees for first-order convex optimization methods, unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The authors aim to show that any first-order method with a primal bound also has an implicit primal-dual guarantee.
method: They use Performance Estimation Problems (PEPs) to analyze fixed-step first-order methods and derive dual certificates.
result: They prove that under mild conditions, a primal bound implies an explicit primal-dual gap bound at the same rate.
conclusion: The work provides a general framework for understanding dual certificates in convex optimization.

title: Learning To Recover: Adaptive Local Branching With Reinforcement Learning For Log-truck Routing And Scheduling Under Disruptions
authors: Abdelhakim Abdellaoui, Issmail El Hallaoui, Loubna Benabbou, Fran\c{c}ois Aub\'e, Mouloud Amazouz
abstract: ArXiv:2607.20901v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the real-time reoptimisation of log-truck routing and scheduling in the Canadian forestry industry following unforeseen disruptions. Road closures, vehicle breakdowns, travel delays, and demand fluctuations invalidate pre-established tactical plans and call for recovery decisions that simultaneously restore feasibility and limit deviation from the original schedule, two objectives inherently in tension under tight time constraints. We formulate recovery as a sequence of neighbourhood-restricted mixed-integer linear programs parameterised by a deviation bound [MATH], the [MATH] distance between the recovered and baseline plans. We show that the minimum feasible value [MATH] can be computed exactly, anchoring the search at its most stable extreme. Rather than targeting a single [MATH], we seek a Pareto front of non-dominated recovery plans spanning the stability--cost space, giving dispatchers a structured set of operational options. To navigate this space efficiently, we propose a reinforcement learning policy, trained with the REINFORCE policy-gradient algorithm, that adaptively selects successive values of [MATH] from solver feedback, concentrating computational effort in productive regions and terminating exploration when further improvement is unlikely. Evaluated on weekly instances derived from historical data of a Canadian forestry partner, under disruption scenarios covering all event categories considered, the approach recovers richer Pareto fronts with fewer solver calls than fixed-[MATH] grid and dichotomic search baselines, and produces feasible recovery plans within operationally acceptable reoptimization times across all configurations and disruption types.
tldr: This paper applies reinforcement learning to optimize log-truck routing and scheduling under disruptions in the forestry industry.
motivation: Real-time reoptimization of log-truck operations is needed to handle unforeseen disruptions like road closures and vehicle breakdowns.
method: The problem is formulated as a sequence of neighborhood-restricted mixed-integer linear programs, and a REINFORCE-based reinforcement learning policy adaptively selects deviation bounds to explore the Pareto front.
result: The approach recovers richer Pareto fronts with fewer solver calls than fixed-grid and dichotomic search baselines, producing feasible plans within acceptable reoptimization times.
conclusion: The proposed method effectively balances stability and cost in recovery planning, offering dispatchers a structured set of operational options.

title: Boundary Control And Periodic Trajectories Of Semilinear Euler Equations With Application To Hydrogen Transport
authors: Peter Benner Alexander Zuyev
abstract: ArXiv:2607.20948v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A mathematical model of gas flow in a pipeline controlled by the inlet pressure and the outlet mass flow flux is considered in the form of the isothermal Euler equations with an appropriate equation of state. Within the framework of boundary control systems, this model is transformed into a nonlinear abstract differential equation using an appropriate lifting operator. For this abstract equation, a representation in terms of Fourier coefficients is derived analytically. Conditions for the existence of periodic solutions to a broad class of nonlinear control systems with continuously differentiable controls are established in abstract spaces. This framework is applied to a realistic hydrogen transport model to evaluate periodic operating regimes under periodic fluctuations in supply and demand.
tldr: This paper studies boundary control and periodic trajectories of semilinear Euler equations applied to hydrogen transport in pipelines.
motivation: To model and control gas flow in pipelines, specifically for hydrogen transport, under periodic supply and demand fluctuations.
method: Transforms the isothermal Euler equations into a nonlinear abstract differential equation using a lifting operator, derives Fourier coefficient representation, and establishes conditions for periodic solutions.
result: Conditions for existence of periodic solutions are derived and applied to a realistic hydrogen transport model.
conclusion: The framework enables evaluation of periodic operating regimes for hydrogen transport under fluctuating conditions.

title: Dynamic Cloud Service-Capacity Deployment With Costly Response Readiness
authors: Ruihan Zhou, Xiaowei Zhang, Yijie Peng
abstract: ArXiv:2607.20961v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI product launches require service-capacity decisions before sufficient product-specific workload histories are available. Early service observations update beliefs about remaining workload, but workload does not physically deplete capacity as inventory demand does. Preserving rapid-response capability may also require costly capacity-access and operational arrangements. We study how a firm should jointly decide current capacity deployment and future response readiness. We formulate a finite-horizon dynamic program with workload beliefs, serviceable capacity, and an absorbing response-channel state. A preservation-deployment decomposition solves one deployment problem for each continuation choice and compares the resulting optimized values. This structure identifies when response readiness should be preserved and how much capacity should be deployed. We operationalize the framework through the Cold-Start Belief Actionability Policy (CBAP), which estimates side-specific values using workload scenarios drawn from predictive beliefs. We also establish bounds on its decision and lifecycle performance losses. Numerical experiments and a BurstGPT-based evaluation show that CBAP reduces lifecycle cost relative to benchmark policies by avoiding premature deployment and unnecessary readiness spending. The results distinguish forecast informativeness from operational actionability and show that current deployment and future response readiness are separate decision margins. Zero deployment may represent Standby rather than Exit, while positive deployment need not imply preserving the response channel.
tldr: This paper studies dynamic service-capacity deployment for AI products under demand uncertainty, using a finite-horizon dynamic program and a Cold-Start Belief Actionability Policy.
motivation: AI product launches require capacity decisions before workload histories are available, and preserving rapid-response capability incurs costs.
method: Formulates a finite-horizon dynamic program with workload beliefs, serviceable capacity, and an absorbing response-channel state; proposes a preservation-deployment decomposition and the CBAP policy.
result: CBAP reduces lifecycle cost relative to benchmarks by avoiding premature deployment and unnecessary readiness spending.
conclusion: Current deployment and future response readiness are separate decision margins; zero deployment may represent standby rather than exit.

title: On The Existence Of Extremizers For The Sum Of Eigenvalues Of Toeplitz Operators
authors: Fabio Nicola, Federico Riccardi, Paolo Tilli
abstract: ArXiv:2607.20965v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that, among all measurable sets [MATH] of prescribed Lebesgue measure, there exists a set maximizing the sum of the first [MATH] eigenvalues ([MATH]) of the associated Toeplitz operator on the Fock space. In the Fock setting, the case [MATH] is well known, the optimal sets being balls of prescribed measure, whereas for [MATH] the existence of optimal sets appears to be new (maximizers are not known explicitly, and the optimality of balls remains conjectural). Moreover, under mild assumptions, our proof extends to localization operators associated with abstract wavelet transforms. In this broader setting, the result is new even for [MATH]. As an application, we prove the existence of optimal sets for the Donoho--Stark concentration problem and its generalization to orthonormal systems.
tldr: This paper proves existence of extremal sets for sums of eigenvalues of Toeplitz operators on Fock space, with applications to the Donoho-Stark concentration problem.
motivation: The problem of maximizing sums of eigenvalues of Toeplitz operators arises in signal processing and time-frequency analysis, but the paper is purely mathematical with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors use variational methods and compactness arguments in the Fock space setting, extending results to localization operators for wavelet transforms.
result: Existence of optimal sets for prescribed measure is established for the sum of the first N eigenvalues, which is new for N>1 in the Fock case and for N=1 in the general wavelet setting.
conclusion: The results provide a rigorous foundation for optimal concentration problems, but have no direct relevance to the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Control Co-design Of Systems With Parabolic Pde Dynamics
authors: Prasad Vilas Chanekar Antika Yadav
abstract: ArXiv:2607.20975v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study the control co-design (CCD) synthesis problem for a class of systems with parabolic partial differential equation (PDE) dynamics. We first derive a sufficient stability condition for the PDE. By spatially discretizing the PDE and using the sufficient stability condition, we propose a computationally tractable approximate CCD problem. We solve the approximate CCD problem using a gradient-based method. Finally, we justify our proposed approach through an example.
tldr: This paper addresses control co-design for systems with parabolic PDE dynamics, which is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: The paper aims to develop a computationally tractable approach for control co-design of systems governed by parabolic PDEs.
method: A sufficient stability condition is derived, the PDE is spatially discretized, and a gradient-based optimization method solves the approximate CCD problem.
result: The proposed method is justified through an example, demonstrating its tractability.
conclusion: The approach provides a practical way to handle control co-design for parabolic PDE systems.

title: Solow System Driven By $\alpha$-stable L\'evy Process
authors: Shenglan Yuan Yiren Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.20997v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper empirically implements a Solow-type growth model driven by [MATH]-stable L\'evy shocks with time-varying capital elasticity. We extend the framework with an [MATH]-stable L\'evy process, thereby capturing three stylized facts of severe macroeconomic fluctuations: heavy-tailed distributions, jump discontinuities, and infinite variance. We derive the stationary distribution of the capital deviation process, obtain its conditional characteristic function in closed form, and provide an integral representation that explicitly reveals a dual mean-reversion structure separating investment gestation lags from endogenous feedback. We design an estimation strategy based solely on well-defined objective functions that respects the probabilistic properties of L\'evy-driven data and circumvents the non-existence of variance. We apply the framework to Argentine quarterly data from 2004 to 2023, with time-varying capital elasticity calibrated from Penn World Table labor shares. Our estimates show that the L\'evy specification delivers structural parameters substantially closer to external PWT benchmarks than the Gaussian Ornstein-Uhlenbeck counterpart and substantially improves crisis-period tracking without sacrificing performance in tranquil periods. Cross-country evidence from Colombia and the United States confirms that the quarterly capital adjustment speed [MATH] exhibits striking stability across vastly different volatility regimes. Robustness checks across tail index specifications demonstrate that the L\'evy framework consistently outperforms the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck benchmark for a broad range of empirically relevant tail indices. These findings establish the L\'evy specification as a robust generalization of the Gaussian benchmark, offering a more credible tool for forecasting and structural parameter estimation in both emerging and advanced economies.
tldr: This paper applies a Solow growth model driven by α-stable Lévy shocks to macroeconomic data, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The authors aim to capture heavy-tailed distributions, jump discontinuities, and infinite variance in macroeconomic fluctuations using Lévy processes.
method: They extend the Solow model with α-stable Lévy shocks, derive the stationary distribution and conditional characteristic function, and design an estimation strategy that avoids variance issues.
result: The Lévy specification yields structural parameters closer to external benchmarks and improves crisis-period tracking compared to Gaussian Ornstein-Uhlenbeck models.
conclusion: The Lévy framework is a robust generalization for forecasting and structural estimation in macroeconomics.

title: Stabilization Of 1d Linear Hyperbolic Balance Laws By Integral Difference Control And Application To Networks Stabilization
authors: Adam Braun (L2S), Jean Auriol (L2S), Lucas Brivadis
abstract: ArXiv:2607.21060v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper develops a unified method for the exponential stabilization of first-order linear hyperbolic balance laws under general actuation, including both underactuated boundary and in-domain control. The proposed framework brings together a wide range of underactuated configurations within a single formulation and substantially extends existing results restricted to particular actuation settings. Using cutting and folding transformations, the proposed approach is further applied to networks of hyperbolic balance laws, including configurations with cycles. The control design is developed under a stabilizability condition and a robustness assumption. It is based on an invertible backstepping transformation, which partially decouples the system, followed by a reformulation of the stabilization problem at the level of an Integral Difference Equation (IDE). The gains of the resulting dynamic feedback law are constructed at the IDE level by combining a stable rank-reduction procedure, which reduces the problem to a single-input design, with the solution of an interpolation equation arising from a Corona problem. Numerical simulations are presented for a relevant cycle network that cannot be addressed by existing methods in the literature.
tldr: This paper develops a unified method for exponential stabilization of first-order linear hyperbolic balance laws using integral difference control, with application to networks including cycles.
motivation: Existing stabilization methods for hyperbolic balance laws are restricted to particular actuation settings, and network configurations with cycles are not addressed.
method: The approach uses cutting and folding transformations, an invertible backstepping transformation to partially decouple the system, and reformulates the stabilization problem as an Integral Difference Equation (IDE). Gains are constructed via a stable rank-reduction procedure and solving an interpolation equation from a Corona problem.
result: The proposed dynamic feedback law achieves exponential stabilization for a broad class of underactuated boundary and in-domain control configurations, including cycle networks that previous methods could not handle.
conclusion: The unified framework substantially extends the applicability of backstepping-based control to complex network topologies, validated by numerical simulations.

title: A Stability-preserving Polytopal Discontinuous Galerkin Method For The Fisher-Kolmogorov Model With Applications To Neurodegenerative Diseases
authors: Paola Francesca Antonietti, Francesca Bonizzoni, Mattia Corti, Nicola de March, Salvatore Di Noto, Francesco Regazzoni
abstract: ArXiv:2607.21108v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Fisher-Kolmogorov model is one of the most widely used models in the study of neurodegenerative diseases, owing to its simple structure as a nonlinear reaction-diffusion equation. In particular, it is commonly employed to describe proteinopathies such as Alzheimer's and Parkinson's diseases. Under suitable assumptions, non-negativity of the solution is guaranteed at the continuous level, which is physically relevant since the solution represents a relative concentration. However, this property is not generally preserved at the discrete level, potentially leading to unphysical and unstable numerical approximations. In this work, we analyze a modified version of the Fisher-Kolmogorov model that stabilizes the dynamics around the unstable equilibrium [MATH]. For the spatial discretization, we adopt a discontinuous Galerkin method on polygonal and polyhedral meshes, coupled with the Crank-Nicolson scheme for time integration. We derive stability and [MATH]-priori error estimates for the semi-discrete problem. The theoretical findings are supported by numerical experiments, including convergence studies in both two and three dimensions. Finally, we validate the model through simulations of [MATH]-synuclein diffusion in a two-dimensional agglomerated brain section, demonstrating the high-order accuracy and robustness of the proposed method.
tldr: This paper presents a numerical method for solving the Fisher-Kolmogorov reaction-diffusion equation applied to neurodegenerative disease modeling.
motivation: The Fisher-Kolmogorov model is used to study proteinopathies like Alzheimer's, but standard numerical methods may violate non-negativity of the solution, leading to unphysical results.
method: A discontinuous Galerkin method on polygonal/polyhedral meshes is combined with a modified Fisher-Kolmogorov model that stabilizes the unstable equilibrium, and Crank-Nicolson time integration.
result: Stability and a priori error estimates are derived for the semi-discrete problem, and numerical experiments in 2D and 3D confirm high-order accuracy and robustness.
conclusion: The proposed method preserves non-negativity and provides accurate simulations for brain protein diffusion, demonstrating its potential for neurodegenerative disease modeling.

title: A Damped Swift Method For European Option Pricing: Coefficients Decay, Truncation, And Error Analysis
authors: Davide Trevisani, Jos\'e Germ\'an L\'opez Salas, Chiheb Ben Hammouda, Cornelis W. Oosterlee
abstract: ArXiv:2607.21109v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a damped variant of the Shannon Wavelet Inverse Fourier Technique (SWIFT) for pricing European options when the characteristic function of the underlying model is available. The key idea is to apply an exponential damping transformation to the payoff, which enables the direct computation of Fourier coefficients in the frequency domain without introducing an additional physical-domain truncation parameter. We provide a rigorous analysis of the decay of these coefficients by exploiting the singularity structure of the associated Fourier transforms. For light-tailed models, we obtain Gaussian-type decay estimates, while for semi-heavy and heavy-tailed models whose singularities are poles, algebraic branch points, or logarithmic branch points, we derive exponential decay bounds with explicit polynomial prefactors. The resulting sharp bounds make it possible to truncate the Fourier series without relying on the cumulants of the underlying density, which are often unavailable or difficult to compute in practice. We further derive an error decomposition separating projection, truncation, and quadrature errors, and translate the analysis into practical rules for selecting the damping parameter, resolution level, and truncation range. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the proposed approach consistently improves the accuracy of the original SWIFT method while requiring a significantly smaller number of Fourier coefficients and remaining stable in cases where the undamped method deteriorates.
tldr: This paper introduces a damped variant of the SWIFT method for pricing European options using characteristic functions, with rigorous error analysis.
motivation: The original SWIFT method requires a physical-domain truncation parameter and relies on cumulants that may be unavailable; the damped variant aims to improve accuracy and stability.
method: An exponential damping transformation is applied to the payoff to compute Fourier coefficients directly in the frequency domain, and sharp decay bounds are derived for various tail behaviors.
result: Gaussian-type decay for light-tailed models and exponential decay with polynomial prefactors for heavy-tailed models are obtained, enabling practical truncation rules.
conclusion: The damped SWIFT method consistently improves accuracy over the original while requiring fewer Fourier coefficients and remaining stable in challenging cases.

title: A Mixed Discrete Cosserat Rod Formulation
authors: Tianxiang Dai, Marco Herrmann, Jonas Breuling, Remco I. Leine, Simon R. Eugster
abstract: ArXiv:2607.21164v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this communication we propose a discrete Cosserat rod formulation in which a slender elastic rod is represented as a chain of rigid bodies (nodes) coupled by compliant elastic forces and moments acting between adjacent node pairs. Discrete dilatation, shear, torsion and curvature strain measures are evaluated from the relative kinematics of each node pair, while the constitutive behavior is expressed in compliance form through independent stress degrees of freedom. We show that the resulting model arises rigorously from a mixed Petrov--Galerkin Cosserat rod finite element formulation (FEM) at linear kinematic interpolation order when the internal virtual work is integrated by the midpoint rule and the external and inertial contributions by the trapezoidal rule. The proposed formulation inherits the robustness and the absence of locking from the underlying mixed FEM while simultaneously exposing a two-node coupling structure that mirrors discrete rod models from the computer graphics community. This is in sharp contrast to the dense coupling of strain-parameterized reduced-order models often used in soft robotic applications. Three numerical examples involving piecewise-varying cross sections, tendon-driven actuation under different spatial discretizations, and coupled longitudinal-torsional dynamics confirm the accuracy, robustness, and convergence behavior of the presented approach.
tldr: This paper presents a mixed discrete Cosserat rod formulation for modeling slender elastic rods, combining finite element methods with discrete rod models.
motivation: To develop a robust, locking-free rod model that bridges the gap between continuum mechanics and discrete rod models used in computer graphics and soft robotics.
method: A mixed Petrov-Galerkin finite element formulation with linear kinematic interpolation, using midpoint rule for internal virtual work and trapezoidal rule for external/inertial contributions, resulting in a two-node coupling structure.
result: The formulation inherits robustness and absence of locking from mixed FEM while exposing a simple two-node coupling, confirmed by numerical examples including piecewise-varying cross sections and tendon-driven actuation.
conclusion: The proposed discrete Cosserat rod formulation is accurate, robust, and converges well, making it suitable for applications in soft robotics and other fields requiring efficient rod modeling.

title: Differentiability Of The Operator Norm On $\ell_p$ Spaces
authors: Sreejith Siju
abstract: ArXiv:2607.21167v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we present a characterization of strong subdifferentiability of the norm of bounded linear operators on [MATH] spaces, [MATH]. Furthermore, we prove that the set of all bounded linear operators in [MATH] for which the norm of [MATH] is strongly subdifferentiable is dense in [MATH]. Additionally, we present a characterization of Frechet differentiability of the norm of bounded linear operators from [MATH] to [MATH], where [MATH]. Applying this result, we will show that the Frechet differentiability and the Gateaux differentiability of the norm of bounded linear operators on [MATH] spaces coincide, extending a known theorem regarding the operator norm on Hilbert spaces.
tldr: This paper studies differentiability properties of the operator norm on ℓ_p spaces, a topic in functional analysis.
motivation: To characterize strong subdifferentiability and Fréchet differentiability of the operator norm on ℓ_p spaces, extending known results from Hilbert spaces.
method: The authors use functional analysis techniques, including properties of ℓ_p spaces and operator theory, to derive characterizations of differentiability.
result: They characterize strong subdifferentiability of the operator norm on ℓ_p spaces and prove that the set of operators where the norm is strongly subdifferentiable is dense. They also show that Fréchet and Gâteaux differentiability coincide for operators on ℓ_p spaces.
conclusion: The results extend classical differentiability results for operator norms from Hilbert spaces to ℓ_p spaces, contributing to functional analysis.

title: Generic Properties Of Planar Symplectic Billiards
authors: Luca Baracco, Olga Bernardi, Jos\'e Pedro Gaiv\~ao
abstract: ArXiv:2607.21223v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study generic properties of planar symplectic billiards, a symplectic analogue of classical Birkhoff billiards introduced by P. Albers and S. Tabachnikov. We prove that, for a residual set of [MATH] strongly convex domains, periodic symplectic billiard trajectories are in general position and non-degenerate. We also prove a Franks' lemma for symplectic billiards and deduce that stably hyperbolic periodic points form a hyperbolic set given by the closure of the set of hyperbolic periodic points. We further show that, for a residual set of [MATH] strongly convex domains, elliptic periodic points are stable and hyperbolic periodic points have transverse homoclinic points. Based on these results, we conclude that --generically-- [MATH] strongly convex symplectic billiard has positive topological entropy.
tldr: This paper studies generic properties of planar symplectic billiards, a dynamical systems topic with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The authors aim to understand the generic behavior of symplectic billiards, an analogue of classical Birkhoff billiards, focusing on periodic trajectories and hyperbolicity.
method: They use techniques from dynamical systems and symplectic geometry, including Franks' lemma and residual set arguments, to prove genericity results.
result: They show that for a residual set of strongly convex domains, periodic trajectories are non-degenerate, elliptic points are stable, and hyperbolic points have transverse homoclinic points, leading to positive topological entropy.
conclusion: The paper concludes that generic strongly convex symplectic billiards exhibit chaotic behavior with positive topological entropy.

title: A Hyper-Reduced Neural Network-Augmented Semi-smooth Newton Method For Nonlinear Parametric Variational Inequalities
authors: Sofiane Ezzehi, Virginie Ehrlacher, Guillaume Ench\'ery, Thibault Faney
abstract: ArXiv:2607.21242v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a model order reduction framework for nonlinear parametrized variational inequalities arising in computational mechanics. The high-dimensional model is written in mixed primal-dual form with projection-based complementarity conditions, leading to nonlinear nonsmooth algebraic systems solved by a semi-smooth Newton method in primal-dual form. On this basis, reduced models are constructed by proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) of both primal and dual solution snapshots, and the resulting reduced systems are solved by semi-smooth Newton iterations in the reduced space. To address cases where low-dimensional linear spaces provide limited approximation efficiency, we introduce a neural-network-augmented reduced model. Two feedforward networks learn corrections in the truncated POD coordinates of the primal and dual variables, defining a nonlinear manifold approximation that is embedded directly in the semi-smooth Newton iterations. The online cost associated with high-dimensional residual evaluations is reduced through hyper-reduction, using a sparse cubature approach based on greedy nonnegative least squares. Particular attention is paid to the interaction between hyper-reduction and the learned nonlinear manifold. The proposed methodology is assessed on two nonlinear variational inequalities with distinct sources of nonlinearity: a two-dimensional obstacle problem with a cubic nonlinearity in the state equation, and a three-dimensional frictional contact problem in which the Coulomb law induces a nonlinear projection in the constraint equation. Numerical results compare the high-dimensional model, the linear reduced model, the neural-network-augmented reduced model, and their hyper-reduced variants, demonstrating accurate approximations with substantial reductions in online computational cost.
tldr: This paper proposes a model order reduction framework for nonlinear parametric variational inequalities using POD and neural network augmentation.
motivation: To efficiently solve high-dimensional nonlinear variational inequalities arising in computational mechanics, which are computationally expensive.
method: Combines proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) with neural network corrections on a nonlinear manifold, and uses hyper-reduction via sparse cubature to reduce online costs.
result: The method achieves accurate approximations with substantial reductions in online computational cost on two test problems.
conclusion: The proposed framework effectively reduces computational cost while maintaining accuracy for nonlinear parametric variational inequalities.

title: A Gaussian Smoothing-based Zeroth-order Method For Goldstein Second-order Stationarity
authors: Ming Lei, Ting Kei Pong, Man-Chung Yue, Liaoyuan Zeng, Hao Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.21258v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a new generalized Hessian, called the Goldstein second-order [MATH]-subdifferential, and an associated notion of [MATH]-second-order stationary point for continuously differentiable functions with locally Lipschitz gradients. We propose a zeroth-order algorithm based on cubic regularization and Gaussian smoothing with homotopy to find such approximate second-order stationary points for Lipschitz differentiable functions, and derive the iteration complexity under a mild coercivity-type assumption on the objective function.
tldr: This paper introduces a zeroth-order optimization method for finding approximate second-order stationary points using Gaussian smoothing and cubic regularization.
motivation: To develop a practical algorithm for nonconvex optimization that can guarantee convergence to second-order stationary points without requiring gradient information.
method: The authors define a generalized Hessian (Goldstein second-order subdifferential) and propose a zeroth-order algorithm combining cubic regularization with Gaussian smoothing and homotopy.
result: Iteration complexity bounds are derived under a mild coercivity-type assumption on the objective function.
conclusion: The proposed method provides a theoretical framework for zeroth-order second-order optimization, but its practical applicability remains to be demonstrated.

title: Adaptive Non-Linear Partition Of Unity Methods For Scattered Data Interpolation With Discontinuities
authors: Adeeba Haider, Roberto Cavoretto, Juan Ruiz-\'alvarez, Dionisio F. Y\'a\~nez
abstract: ArXiv:2607.21287v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Scattered data approximation with discontinuities is challenging due to the Gibbs phenomenon, which significantly reduces accuracy near interfaces. The recently introduced Non-Linear Partition of Unity Method (NL-PUM) addresses this by combining Radial Basis Function (RBF) interpolation with a non-linear Weighted Essentially Non-Oscillatory (WENO) strategy. While effective, NL-PUM's performance relies heavily on two fixed hyperparameters: the RBF shape parameter and the patch radius. This work extends NL-PUM by adapting both hyperparameters locally using Leave-One-Out Cross-Validation (LOOCV) minimized via Global Optimization with Optimistic Improvement (GOOI). Our main innovation is a smoothness indicator linking a discontinuity-aware shrinkage process to LOOCV-based radius selection: patches in smooth regions remain unchanged, while those near discontinuities automatically shrink to avoid crossing the interface. The resulting method, LOOCV-NL-PUM-GOOI, requires no prior knowledge of interface geometry and introduces no extra cost beyond standard adaptive shape parameter selection. Numerical experiments on synthetic test functions with jump discontinuities and a real-data application to Norwegian Fjords elevation data confirm that this approach substantially reduces approximation error near discontinuities while preserving full accuracy in smooth regions.
tldr: This paper presents an adaptive non-linear partition of unity method for scattered data interpolation with discontinuities, using cross-validation and global optimization to tune hyperparameters.
motivation: Scattered data approximation near discontinuities suffers from the Gibbs phenomenon; existing methods require manual tuning of hyperparameters.
method: The authors extend the Non-Linear Partition of Unity Method by locally adapting the RBF shape parameter and patch radius via Leave-One-Out Cross-Validation minimized with Global Optimization with Optimistic Improvement.
result: The method reduces approximation error near discontinuities while maintaining accuracy in smooth regions, demonstrated on synthetic and real-world elevation data.
conclusion: The proposed LOOCV-NL-PUM-GOOI method effectively handles discontinuities without prior knowledge of interface geometry and with no extra computational cost beyond standard adaptive parameter selection.

title: An Unfitted Boundary Algebraic Equation Method With Calder\'on Preconditioning For 2d Stokes Flow In Irregular Geometry
authors: Qing Xia Wenjun Ying
abstract: ArXiv:2607.21295v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present an unfitted boundary algebraic equation method for the two-dimensional exterior/interior Stokes equations on a staggered MAC grid. By constructing an explicit free-space pair of velocity and pressure lattice Green's functions (LGFs) from free-space Laplace LGFs, we represent homogeneous fields using sources supported exclusively on thin staggered boundary layers. This formulation imposes physical Dirichlet data at cut points via local interpolation, while sampled-normal rank updates remove hydrostatic null modes associated with single or multiple obstacles. The workflow parallels that of classical boundary integral formulations and requires no artificial boundary conditions for exterior flows, but follows a discretize-then-represent route and does not require singular/near-singular quadrature. The resulting dense boundary system is solved via GMRES, utilizing a componentwise discrete Calder\'on preconditioner built from the scalar Laplace kernel and padded FFTs for fast volume convolutions. Extensive numerical validation, including multiply connected domains, narrow gaps, and Moffatt eddies, confirms discrete incompressibility to solver accuracy and recovers the expected Moffatt eddy scaling. We achieve second-order velocity and pressure convergence and bound maximum discrete divergence within numerical accuracy. The discrete Calder\'on preconditioner reduces the condition number by orders of magnitude and yields nearly mesh-independent conditioning in exterior configurations, while remaining effective---though more demanding---for narrow-gap and fine-grid interior problems.
tldr: This paper presents a numerical method for solving Stokes flow equations in irregular geometries using an unfitted boundary algebraic equation approach with Calderón preconditioning.
motivation: Efficient and accurate simulation of Stokes flow in complex geometries is important for many applications, but existing methods often require conforming meshes or suffer from conditioning issues.
method: The method constructs free-space lattice Green's functions on a staggered MAC grid, represents homogeneous fields via sources on thin boundary layers, imposes Dirichlet data via local interpolation, and uses a discrete Calderón preconditioner to improve conditioning of the dense boundary system solved with GMRES.
result: Numerical tests show second-order convergence for velocity and pressure, discrete incompressibility to solver accuracy, and significant condition number reduction with the preconditioner, even for multiply connected domains and narrow gaps.
conclusion: The proposed method is effective for 2D Stokes flow in irregular geometries, offering a viable alternative to traditional boundary integral methods without requiring singular quadrature or artificial boundary conditions.

title: Electromagnetic-Aware Fluid Antenna Array
authors: Zhentian Zhang, Yuanhui Wu, Hao Jiang, Zhen Chen, Zaichen Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.21375v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fluid antenna arrays (FAAs) offer a promising means of exploiting spatial degrees of freedom through adaptive port positioning. However, most existing communication models treat antenna ports as independent channel samples and therefore overlook the electromagnetic coupling that fundamentally governs compact apertures. This paper develops an electromagnetic-aware current-domain framework for planar FAAs. The proposed model integrates position-dependent multiport impedance, mutual coupling, radiated and accepted power, source-voltage feasibility, and channel variations into a unified baseband-compatible description. The framework is implementation-agnostic: the closed-form half-wave-dipole model adopted in this paper is only one instance and can be replaced by full-wave, measured, or surrogate impedance and embedded-pattern models. Building on this framework, we formulate two optimization-oriented design problems. The first addresses single-beam superdirective beamforming through the joint optimization of port currents and positions under sidelobe, current, voltage, and geometry constraints. The second maximizes the multi-user weighted sum rate via current-domain precoding and position optimization under accepted-power, current, voltage, and spacing constraints. In both cases, the electromagnetic model is not applied as an after-design correction, but is incorporated directly into tractable alternating algorithms with convex current or precoding subproblems and reduced-gradient geometry updates. Simulation results demonstrate that, when properly modeled, mutual coupling can be exploited as a valuable design resource, enabling lower sidelobes and persistent sum-rate gains over fixed-grid and random fluid-antenna benchmarks.
tldr: This paper develops an electromagnetic-aware current-domain framework for planar fluid antenna arrays, incorporating mutual coupling and position optimization for beamforming and multi-user communications.
motivation: Existing fluid antenna models ignore electromagnetic coupling, which is crucial for compact apertures. The authors aim to integrate mutual coupling into a unified framework for realistic performance optimization.
method: They propose a closed-form half-wave-dipole model that captures position-dependent impedance, mutual coupling, and power constraints, and formulate two optimization problems (superdirective beamforming and multi-user sum-rate maximization) solved via alternating algorithms.
result: Simulations show that properly modeled mutual coupling can be exploited to achieve lower sidelobes and persistent sum-rate gains over fixed-grid and random fluid-antenna benchmarks.
conclusion: The electromagnetic-aware framework enables tractable optimization that leverages mutual coupling as a design resource, improving performance in fluid antenna systems.

title: Jordan Algebras, Hemiplex Numbers, And The Cholesky Decomposition Of Arbitrary Symmetric Matrices
authors: Timothy E. Holy Alan Edelman
abstract: ArXiv:2607.21383v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Positive-semidefinite matrices are most efficiently factored using the Cholesky decomposition. For indefinite matrices, the Cholesky factorization does not exist, and the alternatives face greater challenges in achieving numeric stability and preservation of banded structure. Here we pursue an analogy between the requirement for positive-semidefinite matrices and the solution of the quadratic equation x^2 = c for c <= 0. It is shown that a non-associative algebra, called the hemiplex numbers, allows the Cholesky factorization to be computed for arbitrary symmetric matrices. Crucially, the hemiplex Cholesky factorization does not require pivoting for its existence or stability, allowing it to preserve banded structure. For singular matrices it produces a parametrization of the null space, and provides opportunity for truncation of nearly-null directions in a manner similar to common usage of the singular value decomposition. The hemiplex Cholesky factorization may be a practically useful addition to the tools for solving symmetric linear equations.
tldr: This paper introduces a non-associative algebra called hemiplex numbers to extend Cholesky decomposition to arbitrary symmetric matrices, enabling factorization without pivoting and preserving banded structure.
motivation: Standard Cholesky decomposition requires positive-semidefinite matrices; indefinite matrices lack a stable, banded-structure-preserving factorization method.
method: The authors draw an analogy to solving x^2 = c for negative c, leading to a non-associative algebra (hemiplex numbers) that allows a generalized Cholesky factorization for any symmetric matrix.
result: The hemiplex Cholesky factorization exists for all symmetric matrices, does not require pivoting, preserves banded structure, and for singular matrices provides a null space parametrization.
conclusion: This factorization could be a practical tool for solving symmetric linear equations, offering advantages over existing methods like pivoted LDL^T or SVD.

title: AuthProbe: Specification-Driven, Multi-Identity Detection Of Broken Object-Level Authorization In Recruitment Api
authors: Jay Barach
abstract: ArXiv:2607.20574v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Broken Object-Level Authorization (BOLA), also known as Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR), has topped the OWASP API Security ranking since 2019 and is the root cause of some of the largest exposures of applicant data in recruitment technology. The defining feature of this flaw class is that a malicious request is byte-for-byte indistinguishable from a legitimate one, which is precisely why web application firewalls and single identity scanners fail to catch it. We present AuthProbe, an open-source, black-box scanner that detects BOLA and IDOR in HTTP APIs by driving its tests from an OpenAPI specification and by acting under two or more identities that the operator controls. AuthProbe discovers, for each identity, the objects that identity legitimately owns, then attempts to read one identity's objects while authenticated as another and confirms a leak by comparing the response against a ground-truth fetch by the true owner. It also walks predictable identifiers to expose enumeration and reports missing authentication and existence oracles. The tool returns a severity-thresholded exit code and machine-readable reports so that it can gate a continuous integration build. On a synthetic recruitment API in which the McHire failure class is reproduced, AuthProbe detects every planted cross-identity read with no false positives on a hardened counterpart, and its running time grows linearly with the number of objects under test. AuthProbe is released under the Apache 2.0 license with an authorized-use guardrail.
tldr: AuthProbe is a black-box scanner for detecting Broken Object-Level Authorization (BOLA) vulnerabilities in HTTP APIs using multiple identities.
motivation: BOLA is a top API security risk, and existing tools fail because malicious requests are indistinguishable from legitimate ones.
method: The tool uses an OpenAPI specification to discover objects per identity, then attempts cross-identity access and compares responses to detect leaks.
result: On a synthetic recruitment API, AuthProbe detected all planted cross-identity reads with no false positives, and runtime scales linearly with object count.
conclusion: AuthProbe provides an effective, open-source solution for automated BOLA detection that can be integrated into CI pipelines.

title: Geometric Configurations Of Perturbed Jailbreak Prompts
authors: Lynn Delcon, Andres Algaba, Vincent Ginis
abstract: ArXiv:2607.20581v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Perturbation techniques that turn unsuccessful jailbreak prompts into successful ones are continuously evolving, constituting a major security threat to LLM safety. In this paper, we investigate the internal representations of such string-level perturbed jailbreak inputs in the small weight models of the Qwen-2.5-1.5B/-3B/-7B-Instruct and Llama-3.2-1B/-3B/-3.1-8B-Instruct families. We select two representation spaces: the last-layer-last-token embedding space and the top-50 next-token probability space. The former space separates prompts based on their spelling and format, while the latter space is effectively one-dimensional but appears more complex to cluster. Within our refusal-dominated answer set we find no behavioral hyperplane in either space. Only the next token "Sure" in the 1.5B Qwen model, and both tokens "," and "\.C\.C" in the 1$ Llama model, display a significant association with a compliant-labeled answer.
tldr: This paper studies geometric configurations of perturbed jailbreak prompts in LLM representation spaces, finding no behavioral hyperplane for refusal.
motivation: Perturbation techniques that turn unsuccessful jailbreak prompts into successful ones pose a major security threat to LLM safety, motivating investigation of internal representations.
method: The authors analyze last-layer-last-token embeddings and top-50 next-token probability spaces of small Qwen and Llama models for string-level perturbed jailbreak inputs.
result: No behavioral hyperplane separating refusal from compliance is found in either space; only a few tokens show significant association with compliant labels.
conclusion: The representation spaces do not exhibit a clear geometric separation for jailbreak detection, suggesting the need for alternative approaches.

title: Enhancing Attack Detection Capabilities In BACnet/IP Networks Using Machine-Learning Models
authors: John D. Hastings Derek Manzella
abstract: ArXiv:2607.20686v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Building Automation Systems (BAS) manage critical building functions using protocols such as BACnet/IP, yet defenders have limited tooling and few labeled datasets for detecting BACnet-specific attacks. This work addresses these gaps through three contributions. First, CISA's Zeek BACnet parser is modified to produce a unified per-packet log, simplifying feature engineering for machine-learning (ML) pipelines. Second, a simulated BACnet/IP testbed is developed using bacpypes3 to model a small commercial HVAC system with physics-based device behavior, schedule-aware controller logic, and per-packet attack labeling. Third, five unsupervised anomaly detection models are evaluated using baseline traffic and six BACnet attack types, including denial of service, reconnaissance, property tampering, and false data injection. Results show that One-Class SVM achieved the strongest overall performance, with an average F1 score of 0.864 across all attacks and F1 scores above 0.99 for high-volume denial-of-service and reconnaissance attacks. Detection is much stronger for high-volume attacks, such as DoS attacks and reconnaissance, than stealthier techniques such as tampering and false data injection, which scored around 77%.
tldr: This paper applies machine learning to detect attacks in BACnet/IP building automation networks.
motivation: Building automation systems lack effective intrusion detection tools and labeled datasets for BACnet-specific attacks.
method: The authors modify a Zeek BACnet parser, build a simulated testbed with bacpypes3, and evaluate five unsupervised anomaly detection models.
result: One-Class SVM achieves an average F1 of 0.864, with high performance on high-volume attacks but lower on stealthy attacks.
conclusion: Unsupervised ML can detect BACnet attacks, but stealthy attacks remain challenging.

title: Buzz To Boom: Detecting Message Progression Vulnerabilities In Electron Applications Via Segmented Directed Fuzzing
authors: Jianjia Yu, Zhengyu Liu, Ziyang Li, Yu Sun, Yinzhi Cao
abstract: ArXiv:2607.20698v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Electron is a popular framework for building cross-platform desktop applications using web technologies. Such applications consist of multiple processes with different privilege levels that communicate via message passing. When inter-process messages carry attacker-controlled inputs, they can propagate across processes and reach privileged APIs, e.g., command execution. Such a message propagation behavior is characterized as Message Progression Vulnerabilities (MPVs). The exploitation of MPVs is challenging because it often requires multiple steps, e.g., first arbitrary code execution in one process via message passing, and then command injection in another process using another message crafted in the first process. To our knowledge, existing works on Electron security only study unsafe configurations and malicious Document Object Model (DOM) content, i.e., they cannot detect or exploit these vulnerabilities that need to be triggered by complex cross-process exploits via message passing. We present Proton, a segmented directed fuzzing framework for detecting MPVs. Our key insight is to decompose end-to-end fuzzing into per-process segments along message-passing boundaries, where the goals of fuzzing each segment are either: (i) reaching a sink in the current process or (ii) propagating the payload to the next process, to enable the exploration of another process. In the second case, the messages seed the corpus of the next segment. Finally, Proton synthesizes crash inputs from each process to validate end-to-end exploits. We evaluate Proton against 589 real-world Electron applications, resulting in 23 zero-day MPVs. Among them, 22 lead to OS command execution, including projects with over 50k GitHub stars. We responsibly disclosed all findings. To date, we have received 13 acknowledgments, 11 fixes, and 11 CVEs, including a bug bounty from Vercel.
tldr: This paper presents a fuzzing framework for detecting message progression vulnerabilities in Electron applications.
motivation: Electron applications are vulnerable to multi-step exploits via inter-process message passing, but existing tools cannot detect such vulnerabilities.
method: Proton decomposes end-to-end fuzzing into per-process segments along message-passing boundaries, using directed fuzzing to reach sinks or propagate payloads to the next process.
result: Proton found 23 zero-day MPVs in 589 real-world Electron apps, with 22 leading to OS command execution, resulting in 11 CVEs.
conclusion: Segmented directed fuzzing is effective at detecting complex cross-process vulnerabilities in Electron applications.

title: Security Vulnerability Patterns In AI-Generated Code: A Cross-Model Comparative Study
authors: John D. Hastings Shanna M. Kahn
abstract: ArXiv:2607.20713v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM-based coding tools enable non-expert users to generate routine automation scripts that may enter enterprise workflows without meaningful security review. This study examines that risk directly. Code was collected from ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot, and Google Gemini using identical prompts across three automation domains. Claude Code performed a standardized vulnerability review. Each identified vulnerability was scored using CVSS v3.1 and mapped to the OWASP Top 10:2021 and the MITRE ATT&CK frameworks. Every script contained exploitable vulnerabilities. Nine of the 17 identified vulnerability classes appeared in code from all three models, while 14 of the 17 vulnerability classes appeared in at least two models. The weighted CVSS scores across platforms differed by less than 10%. The risk is not tied to any particular model but rather to the task category. Organizations should therefore ask not which tool to trust, but instead whether LLM-generated automation code should be deployed without review.
tldr: This paper studies security vulnerabilities in AI-generated code across multiple LLMs, finding that all models produce exploitable code and the risk is tied to task category rather than model.
motivation: LLM-based coding tools are used by non-experts to generate automation scripts that may bypass security review, posing a risk to enterprise workflows.
method: Code was collected from ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot, and Google Gemini using identical prompts across three automation domains, then reviewed by Claude Code for vulnerabilities scored with CVSS v3.1 and mapped to OWASP and MITRE frameworks.
result: Every script contained exploitable vulnerabilities; 9 of 17 vulnerability classes appeared in all three models, and weighted CVSS scores differed by less than 10% across platforms.
conclusion: The risk is not model-specific but task-specific, so organizations should not deploy LLM-generated automation code without review.

title: Leaky Language Models: Stealing Architecture And Inference Optimizations Via Per-Token Timing
authors: Sadegh Majidi, Niloofar Mireshghallah, Kazem Taram
abstract: ArXiv:2607.20723v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work presents LeakyLMs, a set of attacks that leak proprietary model, architecture, and deployment information from production language models.
